tire_families.notes: Alpha H1 is current and widely sold in India (Apollo product page, Amazon.in, Flipkart, tyremarket.com). SIZE CONTRADICTION: our DB row is 180/55ZR17 rear, but no 180/55ZR17 Alpha H1 exists in any listing — published lineup is 110/70(Z)R17 front and 150/60(Z)R17 rear (plus R-rated variants). Our 180/55ZR17 row appears to be a fabricated size. TyrePlex quotes overall price range Rs 4,974-6,397 (https://www.tyreplex.com/apollo-tyres/alpha-h1).

MODEL NAME WRONG: no 'AM23A Drag Radial' exists. The real tire is the Avon AM23 — a REAR-only, bias, race-use-only (non-DOT) classic ROAD-RACE tire, not a drag radial. Published sizes: 130/65-18, 130/80-17, 150/70-18, 170/60-18, 180/55-18, 130/70R-18 (demon-tweeks.com/us/avon-am23-motorcycle-tyre-2016136) — neither of our sizes (120/70ZR17 front, 180/55ZR17 rear) exists; the front counterpart is the AM22. Still listed at US retailers (RevZilla https://www.revzilla.com/motorcycle/avon-am23-rear-race-tire, Cycle Gear https://www.cyclegear.com/tires/avon-am23-rear-race-tire) but absent from Avon's 2025 EU relaunch lineup (only Cobra Chrome, Spirit ST, 3D Supersport, Roadrider MkII per https://www.tyrepress.com/2026/02/avon-becomes-a-purely-motorcycle-tyre-brand/) — likely running-stock/limited production. No Indian retail channel found; DB india=1 is dubious. No concrete price extractable (retail pages blocked).

Current — one of only four models in Avon's 2025 relaunch (now made in Montlucon, France after Melksham factory closed Dec 2023; sources: https://www.tyrepress.com/2026/02/avon-becomes-a-purely-motorcycle-tyre-brand/, https://twotyres.co.uk/avon-motorcycle-tyre-production-2025/). COMPOUND CONTRADICTION: our DB classes it 'drag_dot' — Cobra Chrome is a CRUISER/touring tire (whitewall options), not a drag DOT tire. RevZilla family price range $170.61-$550.44 depending on size. No Indian retail listing found; DB india=1 dubious.

MODEL NAME WRONG: AM26 is the 'Roadrider', not 'Roadrunner'. The AM26 Roadrider is no longer made (forum + retailer confirmation: https://www.triumphrat.net/threads/avon-roadriders-am26-superceded.970111/, https://twotyres.co.uk/product/avon-roadrider-mk-2/); successor is the Roadrider MkII, which is current and part of Avon's 2025 relaunch (31 sizes, 15"-21", H/V-rated classic bias tire). SIZE CONTRADICTION: our 120/70ZR17 + 180/55ZR17 radial supersport sizes never existed in the AM26/MkII classic range. Compound 'sport' also wrong — classic sport-touring bias. No Indian retail channel found.

'Battlax' alone is Bridgestone's sport tire FAMILY name, not a purchasable model — these 11 rows (mostly small Indian-fitment sizes like 130/70R17, 140/70R17, 150/60-17 at flat Rs 12,000) cannot be verified or priced without a sub-model (BT-39, BT46, S22, SC, etc.). The BT-39 (the likely small-size sport model, e.g. 140/70-17 66H rear) is current (https://www.bridgestone.com/products/motorcycle_tires/products/detail/pr016) but no India pricing surfaced. Battlax line as such is current and sold in India (S22 on amazon.in). Recommend re-tagging these rows with real sub-model names before pricing.

Recommend renaming these rows to SportRad ST; DB Rs 7,800 for the 190/55 is inside the SportRad quoted band.

No Continental tire named 'ConmiTour' exists - name appears garbled. Continental's road products in 180/55ZR17 are Conti Motion / ContiRoadAttack 4 (e.g. https://www.americanmototire.com/street-cruiser-touring/continental-conti-motion-180-55zr-17-73w-rear-02550200000-mc.html ). The similarly-named real product 'ContiTour' is a bias-ply cruiser touring tire (16-inch Harley sizes) and is NOT made in 180/55ZR17. Row needs re-identification (most likely intended: Conti Motion 180/55ZR17).

'ContiTwins' is a real Continental line but it is a vintage/classic-bike tire family (RB2/K112 style, inch and small metric vintage sizes) - it is NOT made in 180/55ZR17, so this row as sized cannot be that product. Continental 180/55ZR17 offerings are Conti Motion / RoadAttack 4 / ContiSportAttack. Row needs re-identification; possibly confused with Conti Twinduro TKC80 (which does exist in 180/55-17 as a dual-sport: https://www.walmart.com/ip/180-55-17-Continental-Conti-Twinduro-TKC80-Tubeless-Dual-Sport-Rear-Tire/35047398 ) but that is an off-road-biased tire, not a 'sport' compound.
